title: Beyond Source Prompts: Towards Visually Grounded AI-Generated Video Quality Assessment
title_zh: 超越源提示：迈向以视觉为基准的AI生成视频质量评估

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in generative artificial intelligence have accelerated video generation technologies. However, AI-generated videos (AIGVs) remain susceptible to various distortions, highlighting the need for dedicated video quality assessment methods. Content semantics play an important role in AIGV quality assessment, with source prompts typically used as textual references. However, these prompts may not accurately reflect the generated video content, resulting in a discrepancy between the intended textual description and the generated result. To address this limitation, this paper proposes VGCap, an AIGV quality assessment framework guided by visually grounded captions that align better with generated content. Specifically, we introduce two forms of captions: a global caption obtained by minimally revising the source prompt based on multi-frame visual evidence, and prompt-independent segment captions that describe localized temporal content. Together, these captions provide complementary textual evidence for assessing spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment. Experimental results on the LGVQ and FETV datasets show that VGCap outperforms representative baselines across all three dimensions. Further ablation studies on caption sources and temporal components confirm the effectiveness of visually grounded captions for each quality dimension, while highlighting the benefits of segment-level features for temporal quality prediction. The source of VGCap will be available at https://github.com/lolo123-123/VGCap .

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in artificial intelligence-generated content have accelerated text-to-video synthesis [ 1 , 2 ] . However, AI-generated videos (AIGVs) often exhibit generation-specific defects, such as malformed objects, content inconsistency, unnatural motion, and semantic deviations from the source prompt [ 3 , 4 ] . These quality defects need to be captured by assessment models, when the AIGVs are evaluated.
paragraphs.zh: 人工智能生成内容的最新进展加速了文本到视频的合成 [1, 2]。 然而，AI 生成的视频（AIGV）常常表现出生成特有的缺陷，例如物体畸形、内容不一致、运动不自然以及与源提示的语义偏差 [3, 4]。 在评估 AIGV 时，这些质量缺陷需要被评估模型捕捉。

sents.en: Recent advances in artificial intelligence-generated content have accelerated text-to-video synthesis [ 1 , 2 ] .
sents.zh: 人工智能生成内容的最新进展加速了文本到视频的合成 [1, 2]。

sents.en: However, AI-generated videos (AIGVs) often exhibit generation-specific defects, such as malformed objects, content inconsistency, unnatural motion, and semantic deviations from the source prompt [ 3 , 4 ] .
sents.zh: 然而，AI 生成的视频（AIGV）常常表现出生成特有的缺陷，例如物体畸形、内容不一致、运动不自然以及与源提示的语义偏差 [3, 4]。

sents.en: These quality defects need to be captured by assessment models, when the AIGVs are evaluated.
sents.zh: 在评估 AIGV 时，这些质量缺陷需要被评估模型捕捉。

paragraphs.en: Video quality assessment (VQA) plays an important role in evaluating perceptual video quality and supporting the optimization of video processing systems [ 5 ] . Previous VQA methods have primarily focused on perceptual distortions in natural or user-generated videos. An early method, VSFA, introduced content-aware features and temporal-memory modeling [ 6 ] . More recent methods, including RAPIQUE and FAST-VQA, integrated statistical and deep features or employed efficient fragment sampling, while DOVER separately modeled technical and aesthetic quality [ 7 , 8 , 9 ] . Although effective for general video distortions, these methods do not explicitly account for generation-specific defects or semantic correspondence with source prompts, limiting their applicability to AIGV quality assessment.
paragraphs.zh: 视频质量评估（VQA）在评估感知视频质量和支持视频处理系统优化方面发挥着重要作用 [ 5 ] 。 以往的 VQA 方法主要关注自然视频或用户生成视频中的感知失真。 一种早期方法 VSFA 引入了内容感知特征和时间记忆建模 [ 6 ] 。 更近的方法，包括 RAPIQUE 和 FAST-VQA，融合了统计特征与深度特征，或采用高效的片段采样，而 DOVER 则分别建模技术质量和美学质量 [ 7 , 8 , 9 ] 。 尽管这些方法对一般视频失真有效，但它们并未显式考虑生成特有的缺陷或与源提示词的语义对应关系，限制了其在 AIGV 质量评估中的适用性。

paragraphs.en: To address these challenges, AIGV quality assessment methods typically consider three complementary dimensions: spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment [ 4 , 10 ] . Existing methods generally adopt multimodal feature fusion and large vision-language models. Feature-fusion methods include Unify Generated Video Quality Assessment (UGVQ) model, which combines visual, motion, and prompt features [ 4 ] , and CRAVE, which jointly models text-video alignment and motion consistency [ 11 ] . Large multimodal model-based methods include AIGV-Assessor, which incorporates spatiotemporal and prompt information into large vision-language models (VLMs) [ 10 ] , and VQ-Insight, which adapts VLMs through progressive video-quality learning [ 12 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 为了应对这些挑战，AIGV质量评估方法通常考虑三个互补的维度：空间质量、时间质量以及文本-视频对齐 [ 4 , 10 ] 。 现有方法普遍采用多模态特征融合和大型视觉-语言模型。 特征融合方法包括统一生成视频质量评估（UGVQ）模型，该模型结合了视觉、运动和提示特征 [ 4 ] ，以及CRAVE，该方法联合建模文本-视频对齐和运动一致性 [ 11 ] 。 基于大型多模态模型的方法包括AIGV-Assessor，它将时空信息和提示信息融入大型视觉-语言模型（VLM） [ 10 ] ，以及VQ-Insight，它通过渐进式视频质量学习来适配VLM [ 12 ] 。

A source prompt describes the intended video content but may not accurately reflect what is actually generated. Consequently, discrepancies between the source prompt and the generated video may limit the effectiveness of prompt-based features in representing the realized content. This motivates the use of visually grounded captions that directly describe the generated content while preserving the source prompt as a reference for the intended semantics.

paragraphs.en: To address these limitations, we propose VGCap, a multidimensional AIGV quality assessment framework that complements the intended semantics of source prompt with visually grounded evidence of the realized video content. VGCap constructs two forms of captions: a global caption obtained by minimally revising the source prompt using multi-frame visual evidence, and prompt-independent segment captions describing localized temporal content. Caption construction is performed offline, decoupling the captioning models from predictor training and inference. Pretrained SigLIP2 [ 13 ] , SlowFast [ 14 ] , and BLIP [ 15 ] encoders extract spatial, motion, and textual features, respectively. Three dedicated branches then fuse the corresponding features to predict spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment. Experiments show that VGCap outperforms representative baselines across all three quality dimensions. Ablation studies confirm that the global caption improves prediction in all three dimensions and that segment-level motion and caption features further improve temporal quality prediction.
paragraphs.zh: 为解决这些局限性，我们提出 VGCap，一个多维度的 AIGV 质量评估框架，它以已实现视频内容的视觉接地证据来补充源提示词的预期语义。 VGCap 构建两种形式的描述文本：一种是通过利用多帧视觉证据对源提示词进行最小程度修改得到的全局描述文本，另一种是与提示词无关、描述局部时间内容的分段描述文本。 描述文本构建在离线状态下进行，从而将描述生成模型与预测器的训练和推理解耦。 预训练的 SigLIP2 [ 13 ]、SlowFast [ 14 ] 和 BLIP [ 15 ] 编码器分别提取空间、运动和文本特征。 随后，三个专用分支融合相应的特征，以预测空间质量、时间质量和文本-视频对齐。 实验表明，VGCap 在全部三个质量维度上均优于代表性基线。 消融研究证实，全局描述文本在所有三个维度上都能提升预测效果，而分段级运动特征和描述文本特征能进一步改善时间质量的预测。

paragraphs.en: The global caption refines the source prompt to better describe the realized video content. For videos with at most 32 frames, all frames are retained; otherwise, 32 frames are uniformly sampled. A prompt-verification model decomposes the source prompt into six components: quantity, subject attributes, subject, action or state, object, and scene. Using only the sampled frames, a visual-description model independently generates descriptions for the same components. The prompt-verification model then verifies each prompt component as supported , contradicted , or uncertain based on frame content. Supported and uncertain components are retained, while contradicted components are replaced with the corresponding verified visual descriptions. The components are recomposed into a global caption while preserving the source-prompt structure.
paragraphs.zh: 全局描述对源提示词进行细化，以更好地描述实际生成的视频内容。 对于最多 32 帧的视频，保留全部帧；否则，均匀采样 32 帧。 提示词验证模型将源提示词分解为六个组成部分：数量、主体属性、主体、动作或状态、对象和场景。 仅使用采样得到的帧，视觉描述模型针对相同的组成部分独立生成描述。 然后，提示词验证模型根据帧内容将每个提示词组成部分验证为「支持」「矛盾」或「不确定」。 「支持」和「不确定」的组成部分予以保留，而「矛盾」的组成部分则替换为相应的已验证视觉描述。 在保留源提示词结构的同时，将各组成部分重新组合成全局描述。

paragraphs.en: Segment captions describe localized temporal content. Videos with fewer than 16, 16–23, 24–31, and at least 32 frames are evenly divided into one, two, three, and four non-overlapping segments, respectively. Up to eight frames are uniformly sampled from each segment. For each segment, the visual-description model generates an initial caption describing the visible subjects, actions or states, objects, and scene. The prompt-verification model verifies the caption against the corresponding frames. If an inconsistency is detected, the visual-description model revises the caption using the verification feedback, followed by a second verification. This frame-only process keeps the segment captions independent of the source prompt and other captions. A binary mask excludes padded segments during training.

We then use three pooling operations to aggregate complementary information across frames, and concatenate and project their outputs to obtain the spatial feature 𝐯 s \mathbf{v}_{s} . paragraphs.en: VGCap is evaluated on the Large-scale Generated Video Quality assessment (LGVQ) dataset [ 4 ] and the Fine-grained Evaluation of Text-to-Video generation (FETV) benchmark [ 20 ] . LGVQ contains 2,808 videos generated by six models from 468 source prompts and provides MOS labels for spatial quality, temporal quality, and text-video alignment. FETV contains 2,476 videos generated by four models from 619 source prompts; its static-quality, temporal-quality, and overall-alignment scores supervise the corresponding VGCap branches. For both datasets, videos sharing the same source prompt are assigned to the same subset. We construct ten prompt-disjoint splits, each using a 7:1:2 training/validation/test ratio. Performance is evaluated using the Spearman rank-order correlation coefficient (SRCC) and Pearson linear correlation coefficient (PLCC) [ 4 ] . Results are averaged over the ten test sets.

paragraphs.en: For a controlled comparison, we focus on encoder-based baselines and exclude assessors built on substantially larger multimodal models. For spatial quality, the baselines include the image quality assessment (IQA) methods UNIQUE [ 21 ] , MUSIQ [ 22 ] , CLIP-IQA [ 23 ] , and LIQE [ 24 ] , together with UGVQ [ 4 ] . For temporal quality, we compare with the VQA methods RAPIQUE [ 7 ] , VSFA [ 6 ] , SimpleVQA [ 25 ] , FAST-VQA [ 8 ] , DOVER [ 9 ] , and UGVQ. Text-video alignment baselines include CLIPScore [ 26 ] , BLIP [ 15 ] , ImageReward [ 27 ] , PickScore [ 28 ] , HPSv2 [ 29 ] , and UGVQ.

paragraphs.en: This paper presented VGCap, a multidimensional AIGV quality assessment framework guided by visually grounded captions. VGCap constructs a global caption from multi-frame visual evidence and prompt-independent segment captions for localized temporal content, to obtain better content awareness. Experiments on LGVQ and FETV show strong performance across all three quality dimensions, with the largest gains in text-video alignment. Ablations confirm that the global caption improves all three dimensions and that segment-level features further enhance temporal quality prediction. These results show that visually grounded captions help assess generated videos based on their actual content. A current limitation is that offline caption construction requires additional VLM inference, increasing computational cost. Future work will explore automated caption verification and more efficient integration of caption construction with quality assessment.
paragraphs.zh: 本文提出了 VGCap，一个由视觉定位字幕引导的多维度 AIGV 质量评估框架。 VGCap 从多帧视觉证据构建全局字幕，并为局部时间内容构建与提示词无关的片段字幕，以获得更好的内容感知能力。 在 LGVQ 和 FETV 上的实验表明，该框架在全部三个质量维度上均表现出色，其中在文本-视频对齐维度上的提升最大。 消融实验证实，全局字幕能提升全部三个维度的表现，而片段级特征能进一步增强时间质量预测。 这些结果表明，视觉定位字幕有助于基于生成视频的实际内容对其进行质量评估。 当前的一个局限是，离线字幕构建需要额外的 VLM 推理，从而增加了计算成本。 未来的工作将探索自动化的字幕验证，以及将字幕构建与质量评估更高效地集成。
